 Guy Ritchie's The Gentlemen is back with an exciting new release.
 The Gentlemen opened in theaters in January 2020, with Ritchie writing, directing, and producing. The story follows an American cannabis wholesaler trying to sell his operation in England, triggering a torrent of blackmail, schemes, and all kinds of dangers. The thriller earned about $126.2 million worldwide against a reported $22 million budget.
 This qualified the crime comedy as a massive success. Helped along by an impressive cast of The Gentlemen , including Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Henry Golding, Michelle Dockery, Jeremy Strong, Eddie Marsan, Colin Farrell, and Hugh Grant, the dramedy left its mark and expanded into a television spinoff led by The White Lotus star Theo James. The spinoff, also titled The Gentlemen , streams on Netflix and has been renewed for season 3.
 Meanwhile, Lionsgate Home Entertainment is releasing the original film on the official 4K + Blu-ray steelbook. The steelbook costs $34.99. It is slated for release just in time for the holidays on December 15 and is currently available for pre-order on Amazon .
 The gallery highlights the Collector's Edition, including the front cover, back, interior, and a close look at the steelbook art, which features McConaughey's character. This is the latest special physical media release from Lionsgate, which has previously unveiled special editions for films as varied as It Follows and La La Land .

 Although there is no direct sequel titled The Gentlemen 2, the story continues as a Netflix spinoff. It follows the movie's premise, centering on an aristocrat who inherits his estranged family’s estate. The only problem is that he soon discovers it's home to Europe’s largest weed farm, bringing complications that have propelled the offshoot to a not-so-common three-season renewal at Netflix. Also, like the original, The Gentlemen 's cast is equally impressive and familiar.
 Along with James, the cast includes Kaya Scodelario ( The Maze Runner ), Giancarlo Esposito ( Breaking Bad ), Ray Winstone ( The Departed ), Hugh Bonneville ( Downton Abbey ), Daniel Ings ( The Crown ), and Michele Morrone ( The Housemaid ), among several others. The series takes place in the same fictional universe as the movie.
 Regarding how The Gentlemen compares to the spinoff show , the earlier version holds a 75% critics' score on Rotten Tomatoes and an 84% audience score. The television show, meanwhile, initially matched the film's score for season 1. But then season 2 proved to be a notable improvement, rising to 86%. Audiences were similarly favorable at 87%.
 A dedicated steelbook release of The Gentlemen and its eventful ending could be the right chance for the movie to build a new audience for the Netflix spinoff, and vice versa, which could, in turn, add momentum to the sequel that's been the subject of speculation.
